headline: Public Law 113-77 extends federal support for the national poison control phone line, a public awareness campaign, and grants to poison control centers through fiscal year 2019.
what_it_does: The law changes the Public Health Service Act to keep funding a nationwide toll-free poison control phone number and a national media campaign about poison prevention through fiscal year 2019. It also renews a grant program for poison control centers and changes the wording from certified to accredited centers. Grant money can now be used to improve communications, data systems, and response capacity so people can reach these centers more easily.

who_it_affects.group: People who need poison control help
who_it_affects.how: The law keeps a toll-free national number and related public information available to people who think someone has been poisoned or exposed to a harmful substance.
Accredited centers may apply for federal grants through fiscal year 2019, and the grant money can pay for upgrades to communications and data systems.
The national media campaign is meant to inform doctors and other providers about poison prevention and local poison center resources.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 24, 2014; the reauthorized programs run through fiscal year 2019.
